text: CITY ATTORNEY IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF MEASURE Q

On May 5, 2026, the Half Moon Bay City Council adopted Ordinance No. 2026-01, approving four agreements between the City of Half Moon Bay ("City") and Mercy Housing California I IO, L.P. ("Mercy"), an affiliate of Mercy Housing California, for the use of City-owned property located at 535 and 555 Kelly Avenue (APNS: 056-150-220 (Partial) and 056-150-200) ("Property") for an affordable housing development for senior agricultural workers and 2,653 square feet of community serving space ("Project").
Measure Q has been placed on the ballot because the City received a petition signed by the requisite number of voters seeking a referendum on Ordinance No. 2026-01.
If approved by the voters, Measure Q would adopt Ordinance No. 2026-01, approving the following four agreements (collectively, "Agreements"):

1. Affordable Housing and Property Disposition Agreement. This agreement governs the pre-development phase and establishes conditions precedent that Mercy must meet before entering into the Ground Lease for the Property with the City. The conditions precedent include, without limitation, requirements regarding Project financing and other construction and development documents.

2. Ground Lease for the Property. This agreement establishes the contractual obligations for leasing the Property and would be for a period of 99 years at a rate of $1 per year. Mercy Housing would be required to, among other things, construct and maintain the improvements on the Property ("Ground Lease"). The Ground Lease also includes specific covenants relating to the affordability restrictions, preference program, and certain terms and conditions for use of the community serving space.
3. Memorandum of Ground Lease. This is recorded against the Property and alerts interested parties of the Ground Lease and where a copy of the Ground Lease may be obtained.

4. Affordable Housing Regulatory Agreement and Declaration of Restrictive Covenants. This agreement and declaration would specify, without limitation, requirements regarding affordability levels for the Project's housing units and are recorded against the Property.

If approved by the voters, Measure Q would adopt Ordinance No. 2026-01 that authorizes the City Manager to execute the Agreements, take actions necessary to implement the Agreements, find the Agreements' approval exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") section 15332 (Infill Projects), make Government Code section 37364 findings, require the City Manager to review the Ground Lease at least every seven years.
A "YES" vote is a vote in favor of Measure Q and in favor of adopting Ordinance 2026-01.
A "NO" vote is a vote against Measure Q and against adopting Ordinance 2026-01.
Measure Q will be effective only if a majority of voters voting on the Measure vote in its favor. The above statement is an impartial analysis of the Measure.
If you desire a copy of the ordinance or measure, please call the City of Half Moon Bay City Clerk's Office at (650) 726-8250 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you.
Denise S. Bazzano City Attorney City of Half Moon Bay

text: YES on 555 Kelly: The fiscally responsible choice This referendum is not about voters choosing whether or not to build 555 Kelly. This is because 555 Kelly is an irreplaceable part of Half Moon Bay's legally required Housing Element and the State has already sued Half Moon Bay to force compliance with State law, including affordable housing projects like 555 Kelly. Your Yes vote will help to ensure that we do not bankrupt the City with fines, penalties and legal costs before the project is finished. What is 555 Kelly? 555 Kelly provides 40 affordable apartments at no cost to taxpayers for senior farmworkers who have worked in our fields for decades. It will include a community center, with a full kitchen, that will be available to the entire community. The project has been fully reviewed and approved. Why your Yes Vote is critical for Half Moon Bay: The financial risks are not hypothetical. The State of California has already sued Half Moon Bay for not meeting our affordable housing requirements. State law bars cities from rejecting housing like this, even by referendum. Courts can force approval anyway, and fine the city up to $10,000 per unit, per month. A No vote could trigger Builders Remedy, which would result in unchecked development being forced on Half Moon Bay, as well as diverting potentially millions in HMB taxpayer money from vital services to pay legal fees, fines and penalties. The bottom line: Under California State law the city must build more affordable housing. Half Moon Bay taxpayers will pay nothing to construct, maintain, or manage 555 Kelly. It's a chance to give back to our senior farmworkers while being fiscally responsible. Your Yes vote can prevent a potentially huge financial loss while helping to solve the city's legal issues instead of making them worse. Please vote YES on Measure VoteYesOn555Ke11y.com
